QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_24

question.text: The DPI (Distributions to Paid-In) multiple of a Category II AIF is BEST interpreted as:

answer.text: A realisation multiple — the cash already returned to investors divided by capital paid in
A measure of unrealised fund value
The NAV per unit at fund inception
A measure of the fund's leverage

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.7.4.2: DPI = Total Distributions / Total Capital Contributions. Called the 'realisation multiple' — it tells LPs how much CASH they have received back per rupee contributed. The Trap: Option B is RVPI. Option C is NAV concept. Option D confuses with leverage. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B tests DPI definition; XXI-B covers DPI for PMS-like closed structures. Manager's Pro-Tip: LPs (especially pension funds) evaluate GPs partly on DPI track records at comparable fund ages. As a GP, delivering early partial distributions — even if sub-optimal from NPV view — boosts DPI optics for your next fundraise.
